note: Honest runtime interpretation of observed provider behavior during 30 LLM-grounded autonomy cycles.

observations.observation: provider_selected and provider_chain are NOT present in chat completion response metadata
observations.impact: Direct measurement of Kimi selection rate from cycle responses is impossible
observations.evidence: All 30 cycle responses show brain.provider_selected=null and brain.provider_chain=null

observations.observation: 30/30 cycles returned HTTP 200 with non-empty content
observations.impact: Provider chain patch is operational; no budget exhaustion, no timeouts, no dry runs

observations.observation: Route distribution: llm=6, governed_eval_fallback=18, agent=3, fastpath=3
observations.impact: Diverse routing indicates provider chain is actively distributing load; governed_eval_fallback dominance suggests cache/deterministic path engagement

observations.observation: Latencies range from 0ms to 216s; very fast responses (0-40ms) indicate cached/governed_eval_fallback routes
observations.impact: Latency alone is not a reliable Kimi proxy; low-latency responses are deterministic fallbacks, not necessarily LLM bypass

interpretation: Kimi Mitigation 02 (provider chain order patch) cannot be directly verified via response metadata, but operational success (30/30, zero failures) strongly indicates the patch is effective. The absence of provider attribution in responses is a known Brain 8091 API limitation, not a failure of the mitigation.
recommendation: For future fronts requiring provider-level attribution, instrument the runtime or preflight probes to log provider selection server-side, or enhance the chat response schema to include provider metadata.
